metadata.scope: Spur, helical, bevel, worm, rack-and-pinion, and planetary gears for 3D printing and light machining.

material_suggestions.use_case: printed or machined gears under moderate load
material_suggestions.notes: Low friction, self-lubricating, dimensionally stable; preferred for plastic gear meshes.

material_suggestions.use_case: functional 3D printed gears with impact resistance
material_suggestions.notes: Good fatigue life; absorbs moisture so dimension allowances needed.
Standard gear steel; can be through-hardened to 50–55 HRC for wear resistance.
Carburize then quench; hard case with tough core. Typical case depth 0.8–1.2 mm.
Easy to machine; softer than steel so only mesh with steel if loads are light.
Sacrificial wear partner for steel worm; good embeddability for contamination tolerance.

standards_used.name: ISO 53 / DIN 867
standards_used.applies_to: basic rack tooth profile for involute spur and helical gears

standards_used.name: DIN 6885A
standards_used.note: Keyway width = shaft_d/4; depth in shaft = width/2.

standards_used.name: AGMA 2101 / ISO 6336
standards_used.applies_to: gear tooth strength and pitting resistance
standards_used.note: Use for load capacity calculations; face width 8–12× module for spur gears.

standards_used.name: Grashof condition
standards_used.note: s + l < p + q for at least one link to rotate fully.

source_references.title: Thingiverse involute gear library (GregFrost thing:3575)
source_references.note: Widely used OpenSCAD involute gear module; basis for parametric gear generation.

source_references.title: gears-master OpenSCAD gear generator examples
source_references.note: Primary local reference for generated gear module names, parameters, assemblies, and example calls.

source_references.title: ISO 53 Basic rack tooth profile
source_references.note: Addendum, dedendum, and pressure-angle rules used throughout this record.

output_policy.openscad_code: Return geometry-only OpenSCAD with named parameters, modules, boolean cuts, and no prose.
forbidden_in_code: string metadata variables such as material, standard_used, or notes

parts.name: Spur gear — module 2, 20 teeth (general purpose)

fit_guidance_mm.bore_clearance: +0.2 to +0.3 for running fit; 0.0 to +0.05 for press fit
fit_guidance_mm.backlash_printed: 0.2–0.3 mm (add to tooth thickness each side)
fit_guidance_mm.keyway_fit: JS9/h9 for sliding; P9/h9 for fixed

tooth_count.label: number of teeth
tooth_count.note: Minimum 14 teeth at 20° pressure angle to avoid undercutting

pitch_diameter.note: do not confuse with bore diameter

center_distance_pair.note: same module and pressure angle required for mesh

keyway_width.note: round down to standard key size: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10 mm

main_features: gear body disk at pitch diameter
involute or simplified tooth profile repeated around pitch circle
hub cylinder extending beyond face width for shaft engagement
shaft bore through hub with clearance
optional keyway slot in bore for torque transmission
optional lightening holes in web for weight reduction
optional set-screw boss perpendicular to bore
design_rules: For plain spur gear output, call gears.scad spur_gear(..., helix_angle=0, optimized=true); do not hand-build rectangular or block teeth.
Always derive pitch_diameter from module and tooth_count, never from bore
Minimum 17 teeth on driving pinion to prevent undercutting at 20° PA
Face width must be 8–12× module for adequate tooth strength
Mating gears must share identical module AND pressure angle
Print gears on their side (teeth horizontal) for best layer-bonding strength
Add 0.2 mm backlash clearance per gear when designing for mesh fit
Hub should extend ≥ 1.5× bore diameter along axis for set-screw grip
Lightening holes must not intrude within 2 mm of root circle
validation_criteria: plain spur gear uses helix_angle=0 unless the user explicitly asks for helical/spiral teeth
pitch_diameter = module × tooth_count (not bore-derived)
outside_diameter = pitch_diameter + 2 × module
root_diameter = pitch_diameter - 2.5 × module
bore subtracted from hub, not from gear disk directly
keyway does not breach hub outer wall (hub_d ≥ bore_d + 2 × keyway_width)
tooth count ≥ 14 (undercutting check)
failure_modes: blocky rectangular or cylinder-lump teeth instead of gears.scad involute-style spur_gear output
using bore_diameter as pitch_diameter — generates undersized gear
placing teeth at root circle instead of pitch circle
omitting hub — shaft grip too weak
keyway depth too deep — bore wall thinner than 1 mm
face width less than 6 mm — tooth snaps under load
non-integer tooth count — module and pitch diameter mismatch

constraint_checks.message: Pitch diameter must equal module × tooth count.
Fewer than 14 teeth causes undercutting at 20° pressure angle.
Face width below 8× module may cause early tooth fatigue failure.

standards_used.name: DIN 6885A parallel key
standards_used.note: Width = shaft_d/4; shaft groove depth = width/2.

material_suggestions.use_case: light-duty printed or machined spur gears
material_suggestions.notes: Self-lubricating; excellent for meshing with steel or aluminium.
Through-harden to HRC 50 for wear life; case-harden 8620 for higher loads.

parts.openscad_module:
include <D:/Downloads/openscad_copilot (1)/openscad_copilot/gears.scad>

spur_gear(
  modul=2,
  tooth_number=20,
  width=10,
  bore=5,
  pressure_angle=20,
  helix_angle=0,
  optimized=true
);

parts.name: Worm wheel — module 2, 30 teeth (1-start worm pair)
main_features: worm wheel disk with helical tooth groove cross-section
throated (concave) rim face to wrap worm
bore and hub for output shaft
worm cylinder with helical thread
design_rules: For worm gear output, call gears.scad worm_gear(...); do not approximate the wheel with simple peg teeth.
Pair worm (steel) with worm wheel (bronze or POM) to manage wear
Self-locking: lead angle < 10° (1 or 2 starts with small module)
Back-driveable: lead angle > 20° (4 starts)
Centre distance must match (worm_pitch_d + wheel_pitch_d) / 2
Worm wheel face width = 2 × worm pitch diameter for full engagement
validation_criteria: centre_distance matches formula
lead angle derived from module, starts, and worm_pitch_diameter
worm and wheel share same module
failure_modes: worm and wheel different modules — no mesh
insufficient lubrication — adhesive wear on bronze wheel
back-driving a self-locking worm — shock load on teeth

constraint_checks.message: Worm and worm wheel must have the same module.

standards_used.name: ISO 53 worm module
standards_used.note: Same preferred module series as spur gears.

standards_used.name: DIN 3975
standards_used.applies_to: worm gear geometry and tooth form
standards_used.note: Defines throated wheel geometry and centre-distance calculations.

material_suggestions.notes: Bronze sacrificial wear partner; good score and embedability.
Self-lubricating POM works well for low-speed low-load worm meshes.

parts.openscad_module:
include <D:/Downloads/openscad_copilot (1)/openscad_copilot/gears.scad>

worm_gear(
  modul=2,
  tooth_number=30,
  thread_starts=1,
  width=22,
  length=30,
  worm_bore=6,
  gear_bore=8,
  pressure_angle=20,
  lead_angle=7.1,
  optimized=true,
  together_built=true,
  show_spur=1,
  show_worm=1
);

parts.name: Straight bevel gear pair - module 2, 20:20 miter gears
main_features: truncated cone gear blank, not a flat cylinder
teeth repeated around the cone and tapered toward the apex
large end has outside diameter, small end is reduced by face_width along pitch cone
hub and bore remain coaxial with each gear shaft
paired gears intersect at the pitch cone apex, usually at 90 degrees
design_rules: Use bevel gears only for intersecting shafts; use worm or hypoid for non-intersecting crossed shafts
For equal miter gears, both pitch angles are 45 degrees
Face width should not exceed one third of cone distance
Both gears must share module, pressure angle, shaft angle, and matching cone apex
Simplified OpenSCAD should show a tapered conical body and tapered teeth, not a spur gear disk
validation_criteria: defines shaft_angle, pitch_angle_pinion, pitch_angle_gear, and cone_distance
uses cylinder with different r1/r2 or d1/d2 for conical bevel body
teeth are repeated with tooth_count and taper from large end to small end
bore is subtracted along the shaft axis
failure_modes: flat spur gear used for a bevel gear request
face width longer than cone distance third, causing pointed weak teeth
gear pair axes offset instead of intersecting at the cone apex

parts.name: Helical / spiral gear - module 2, 24 teeth, 20 degree helix

handed_pair.formula: parallel shaft gears need opposite helix hands

main_features: cylindrical gear with teeth twisted across face width
helix hand parameter: left or right
hub, bore, optional keyway, and lightening holes like a spur gear
paired helical gears have smoother contact but generate axial thrust
design_rules: Use normal module and normal pressure angle as real gear design inputs
Derive transverse module from normal_module / cos(helix_angle)
Keep printed helix angle around 15 to 25 degrees for strength and clean teeth
Add thrust washers or bearings in the surrounding assembly because helical gears create axial load
For double-helical or herringbone gears, mirror the helix at the center to cancel thrust
validation_criteria: defines helix_angle and normal_module
derives transverse_module and pitch_diameter
uses linear_extrude(twist=...) or equivalent stepped rotation for spiral teeth
states or models opposite helix hands for a mating pair
failure_modes: calling a spur gear a spiral gear without tooth twist
using spur pitch diameter formula without helix correction
forgetting axial thrust support in helical mesh

parts.name: Spiral bevel gear pair - module 2, 16:32, 90 degree shafts
standards: ISO 23509 bevel and hypoid gear geometry

tooth_spiral_sweep.formula: spiral_angle controls curved tooth rotation across face

main_features: bevel gear cone body plus curved/spiral teeth
teeth sweep around the cone rather than staying straight radial
pinion and gear pitch cones intersect at common apex
higher contact ratio and smoother operation than straight bevel gears
hub, bore, and mounting flange or bolt circle for real assemblies
design_rules: Represent simplified spiral bevel teeth by rotating tooth features progressively along cone height
Use spiral angle around 30 to 35 degrees for realistic automotive-style geometry
Face width stays below one third cone distance
Both gears must share module, pressure angle, shaft angle, and compatible spiral hand
Do not model as a flat helical gear; it needs both cone taper and spiral tooth sweep
validation_criteria: defines spiral_angle, pitch angles, and cone_distance
uses tapered conical bodies
tooth placement includes both angular repetition and twist/sweep across face
has separate pinion and gear members with correct ratio
failure_modes: missing cone taper
missing spiral tooth sweep
using identical straight bevel logic for a spiral bevel request

parts.name: Planetary gear set - module 1, sun 18, three planets 24, ring 66

planet_spacing_rule.formula: (sun_teeth + ring_teeth) must divide cleanly by planet_count for equal phasing

main_features: central sun gear with external teeth
multiple planet gears equally spaced on carrier pins
internal ring gear with inward-facing teeth
carrier plate with pin bosses and bearing/bushing holes
coaxial input/output shaft bores
design_rules: Ring tooth count must equal sun_teeth + 2 * planet_teeth for same module mesh
Planet centers sit at radius module * (sun_teeth + planet_teeth) / 2
Use at least three planets for balanced load sharing
Internal ring teeth point inward; do not model the ring as an external spur gear
Give planets clearance from carrier plate and add pin holes or bearing seats
For fixed ring, reduction ratio is 1 + ring_teeth / sun_teeth
validation_criteria: defines sun_teeth, planet_teeth, ring_teeth, and planet_count
computes ring_teeth = sun + 2*planet or validates that relationship
places planets with cos/sin on carrier_pin_circle_radius
models ring gear as internal teeth or subtractive tooth gaps inside annulus
includes a carrier plate with planet pin holes
failure_modes: ring tooth count not compatible with sun and planets
planet centers placed by eye instead of formula
external ring gear teeth instead of internal annulus teeth
no carrier pins, so the assembly is not a planetary gearbox
